activities.description: Speaker talks about intangible added value and uses the cereal 'Shreddies' as an example.

characterInteraction.description: The speaker addresses the audience directly.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The speaker highlights the power of perception and how a simple idea can transform a product's value without any physical changes.

mood.description: Excited - Speaker delivers his speech with enthusiasm and hand gestures.

keyMoments.changeDescription: Visual change from a more generic background to a TED stage adds to the excitement of the presentation.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker introduces the concept of intangible added value and teases an interesting case study using Shreddies cereal.

scenes.title: Scene 1

videoEditingDetails.description: The background switches from purple to a TED stage.

activities.description: Factory workers inspect Shreddies cereal moving on a conveyor belt. They look concerned as they notice something different.
The Executive examines the cereal and questions if any 'diamond-shaped' Shreddies have been shipped.

characterInteraction.description: Factory workers communicate nonverbally, indicating their concern.
The Executive asks a question to confirm if the change has been implemented.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The scene suggests that even a seemingly insignificant change like the shape of cereal can cause confusion and raise questions.

mood.description: Confused - The factory workers and executive seem perplexed by the change in Shreddies' shape.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The black and white filter transitions to color as the Executive questions the shape.
Transition to a bright yellow background and upbeat music creates a positive shift as the new Diamond Shreddies are introduced.

narrativeProgression.description: The scene reveals a change in the Shreddies cereal - from square to diamond.

props.name: Conveyor belt with Shreddies cereal, Shreddies cereal boxes

scenes.title: Scene 2

videoEditingDetails.description: Black and white filter creates a dramatic effect.

Transition to a yellow background with the 'Diamond Shreddies' logo and a side-by-side comparison of the old square Shreddies and the new diamond Shreddies. A woman then appears in a kitchen, endorsing the new Diamond Shreddies.

activities.description: Speaker returns to the stage and comments on the effectiveness of the Diamond Shreddies campaign, emphasizing the power of a simple idea and the role of market research.

characterInteraction.description: The speaker engages the audience, eliciting a humorous response.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The audience's laughter suggests an understanding of the ridiculousness of the campaign, highlighting the persuasive power of marketing.

mood.description: Humorous - The audience reacts with laughter and applause as the speaker playfully acknowledges the absurdity of the campaign's success.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The mood shifts from the curiosity of the previous scene to humor as the audience laughs at the speaker's comments.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker confirms the effectiveness of the campaign despite its simplicity. He also hints at the importance of market research.

scenes.title: Scene 3

activities.description: The Focus Group Leader presents the new Diamond Shreddies box to the participants.
Participants express confusion and amusement at the diamond shape.
The Focus Group Leader explains the concept and compares it to the visual illusion of a '6' and '9'.
Participants taste test both the square and diamond Shreddies. They all prefer the diamond-shaped Shreddies, despite the cereal being identical.

characterInteraction.description: The Focus Group Leader facilitates the discussion, and participants openly share their reactions.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The taste test reveals the power of suggestion and how easily our perceptions can be influenced by marketing techniques.

mood.description: Curious - Participants show initial confusion followed by amusement as they engage in the taste test.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The mood shifts from amusement to more serious as the Focus Group Leader tries to rationalize the concept.
The mood becomes more lighthearted again as they begin the taste test.

narrativeProgression.description: The scene demonstrates the effectiveness of the Diamond Shreddies campaign by showing how consumers perceive a difference in taste simply because of the shape.

props.name: Diamond Shreddies box, Shreddies cereal box, trays with square and diamond Shreddies.

scenes.title: Scene 4

climax.description: The taste test results show that the participants preferred the diamond-shaped Shreddies, despite the cereal being identical to the square Shreddies. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the marketing campaign in influencing consumer perception.

storylines.description: The successful marketing campaign of Diamond Shreddies, highlighting the power of intangible added value through a change in perception.

youtube_description:
Rory Sutherland presented this excerpt in his TedTalk (Link Below) where he described on of the most perfect case of creating intangible, added value, without changing the product in the slightest. 

Shreddies is a strange, square, whole-grain cereal, only available in New Zealand, Canada and Britain. A young copywriter named Ogilvy Canada called Hunter Somerville working out how you could re-launch Shreddies. He came up with this unique play on the existing product. A simple view of the product at a 45 degree angle invented the 'Diamond Sherrdie'. A debate raged and unsurprisingly, there were those who actually resented this intrusion. So, eventually, the manufacturers actually arrived at a compromise, which was the combo pack.

Quirky? Yes. Successful? Absolutely.
